claims.text: Conventional EAM reference potentials cannot fully represent the broad spectrum of atomic configurations sampled by an ab initio multicomponent-alloy liquid.
A machine-learning potential trained on diverse ab initio liquid and high-temperature solid configurations can be used as the reference state for thermodynamic integration.
MTP or Gaussian Approximation Potential frameworks are suitable candidate ML-IAP frameworks for this intervention.
The proposed ML-IAP will represent diverse local environments, short-range order, and high-temperature fluctuations more accurately than a conventional EAM potential.
Training on a large database of ab initio configurations enables the ML potential to interpolate among diverse liquid environments.
Improved representation of local environments will increase phase-space overlap between the ML reference and the ab initio target.
Increased reference–target phase-space overlap will reduce artificial thermodynamic-integration path mismatch.
Reduced thermodynamic-integration path mismatch will produce a more direct and accurate free-energy evaluation.
Relative to TOR-TILD calculations using EAM references, the ML reference is expected to reduce path mismatch by approximately 30–50%.
The improvement should yield closer agreement between integrated free energies obtained with the ML reference and independently computed ab initio free energies.
The method is applicable to high-entropy alloys having four or more principal elements and substantial atomic disorder.
The proposed application range is near or above 0.9–1.0 times the alloy melting temperature.
Liquid configurational diversity is pronounced near or above 0.9–1.0 times the melting temperature.
The advantage of the ML reference should diminish for nearly pure elements or simple binary alloys because their liquids have less configurational diversity.
The advantage should also diminish at temperatures substantially below the melting point.
Initial studies in pure and binary systems indicate that ML potentials provide superior phase-space representation.
The exact mismatch reduction in multicomponent HEAs is not yet quantified and is system-dependent.
A controlled comparison should hold simulation cell size, temperature, and composition constant between the EAM-reference and ML-reference integration paths.
The hypothesis is falsified if the ML reference fails to improve phase-space-overlap metrics or fails to reduce benchmark-relative mismatch by at least 30% compared with the EAM reference.
